semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Graph theory in biology has a strong overlap with biological knowledge graphs, focusing on applications of graph theory to biological contexts.

parent_domains.justification: The concept of biological knowledge graphs falls under the broader category of knowledge graphs, which deal with graph-based representation of data.
Biological knowledge graphs are often constructed and utilized within the context of machine learning for biology to uncover insights from biological data.
Biological knowledge graphs are a tool within computational biology, which involves computational and mathematical modeling of biological systems.

closest_parent_domain.justification: As a structured representation of information in graphs, biological knowledge graphs most closely align with the domain of knowledge graphs.

child_domains.justification: A specific type of biological knowledge graph focuses on the regulation of genes, which forms the basis of gene regulatory networks.
This involves computational methods specifically targeted at inferring or constructing gene regulatory networks from data, often modeled as knowledge graphs in the biological domain.

closest_child_domain.justification: Among the child domains, gene regulatory networks are specific instances of biological knowledge graphs focusing on gene interactions.

sibling_domains.justification: Like biological knowledge graphs, temporal knowledge graphs are a specialization of knowledge graphs, focused more on temporal aspects of data.
This focuses on extracting inferences from partial data within knowledge graphs, similar to reasoning in biological contexts.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Temporal knowledge graphs are closely related due to their structural properties and utility in storing domain-specific data over time, similar to biological knowledge graphs.

unrelated_domains.justification: While bioinformatics can benefit from biological knowledge graphs, it is a broader domain involving many computational techniques beyond graph-based methods.
Biology is a broad field, whereas biological knowledge graphs are specific computational tools used within biology.
Graph reasoning generally applies beyond biological contexts to a wider range of graph-based data inquiry.
This is a very broad category that can apply to any domain that uses graph structures.
Though it can apply biological knowledge graphs, biomedical informatics covers a wider range of data and methodologies, not strictly graph-based.
